claim: L-type Ca2+ channels (LTCC or CaV1 channels) play pivotal roles in numerous physiological functions by mediating Ca2+ influx and membrane excitability.
source: L-type Ca2+ channels (LTCC or CaV1 channels) play pivotal roles in numerous physiological functions by mediating Ca2+ influx and membrane excitability (Striessnig et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Striessnig et al., 2014

claim: CaV1.3 channels exhibit unique biophysical properties involving diverse regulatory mechanisms.
source: Among four isoforms of CaV1.1–CaV1.4 in LTCC family, CaV1.3 channels exhibit unique biophysical properties (Lieb et al., 2014; Xu and Lipscombe, 2001) involving diverse regulatory mechanisms (Ben-Johny and Yue, 2014; Christel and Lee, 2012; Huang et al., 2012; Tan et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: CaV1.3 is widely distributed in various excitable tissues, including both cardiovascular and nervous systems.
source: Widely distributed in various excitable tissues, including both cardiovascular and nervous systems (Brandt et al., 2003; Mangoni et al., 2003; Nemzou et al., 2006; Striessnig, 2007), CaV1.3 is also involved in a wide spectrum of pathology, including multiple inheritable diseases (Pinggera and Striessnig, 2016; Platzer et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: CaV1.3 is involved in a wide spectrum of pathology, including multiple inheritable diseases.
source: Widely distributed in various excitable tissues, including both cardiovascular and nervous systems (Brandt et al., 2003; Mangoni et al., 2003; Nemzou et al., 2006; Striessnig, 2007), CaV1.3 is also involved in a wide spectrum of pathology, including multiple inheritable diseases (Pinggera and Striessnig, 2016; Platzer et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citations to Pinggera and Striessnig, 2016; Platzer et al., 2000

claim: CaV1.3 expressed in substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) neurons tightly controls the autonomous subthreshold Ca2+ oscillations which have been considered to underlie the pathophysiology of Parkinson's disease (PD).
source: As one prominent exemplar of its pathophysiological linkage, CaV1.3 expressed in substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) neurons tightly controls the autonomous subthreshold Ca2+ oscillations which have been considered to underlie the pathophysiology of Parkinson's disease (PD) (Chan et al., 2007; Guzman et al., 2009, 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chan et al., 2007; Guzman et al., 2009, 2010

claim: CaV1.3 is tuned by its own distal carboxyl tail (DCT) to compete with apoCaM (Ca2+-free calmodulin), which is pre-associated with the carboxyl terminus of the channel at preIQ3-IQ domain (denoted as IQV).
source: CaV1.3 is tuned by its own distal carboxyl tail (DCT) to compete with apoCaM (Ca2+-free calmodulin), which is pre-associated with the carboxyl terminus of the channel at preIQ3-IQ domain (denoted as IQV).
evidence: This is a statement of the mechanism being studied, supported by the experimental work in the manuscript

claim: IQV plays important roles in channel functions and is closely involved in both apoCaM and Ca2+/CaM binding.
source: Closely involved in both apoCaM and Ca2+/CaM binding (Jurado et al., 1999), IQV plays important roles in channel functions (Ben Johny et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2010; Singh et al., 2006; Wahl-Schott et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: The competitive tuning is highly regulated by fluctuations of [apoCaM], the strength of particular DCT isoforms, or the apoCaM affinity with IQV.
source: The competitive tuning is highly regulated by fluctuations of [apoCaM], the strength of particular DCT isoforms, or the apoCaM affinity with IQV (Adams et al., 2014; Bazzazi et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Adams et al., 2014; Bazzazi et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2010

claim: DCT consists of two putative α-helical domains—a proximal and a distal C-terminal regulatory domain (termed PCRD and DCRD, respectively).
source: DCT consists of two putative α-helical domains—a proximal and a distal C-terminal regulatory domain (termed PCRD and DCRD, respectively) (Hulme et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hulme et al., 2006

claim: Positively charged PCRD could coordinate with negatively charged DCRD, in the context of CaV1.3, to regulate effective CaM affinity to the IQV region of the channel.
source: Positively charged PCRD could coordinate with negatively charged DCRD, in the context of CaV1.3 (Liu et al., 2010), to regulate effective CaM affinity to the IQV region of the channel.
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2010

claim: DCT inhibits Ca2+-dependent inactivation (CDI).
source: Besides the reported inhibition on Ca2+-dependent inactivation (CDI) (Liu et al., 2010; Singh et al., 2006; Wahl-Schott et al., 2006), several studies suggest that DCT also concurrently attenuates voltage-gated activation (VGA), reducing the maximum open probability and positively shifting the voltage dependence (Hulme et al., 2006; Lieb et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2016; Scharinger et al., 2015; Singh et al., 2008; Wahl-Schott et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Liu et al., 2010; Singh et al., 2006; Wahl-Schott et al., 2006

claim: DCT concurrently attenuates voltage-gated activation (VGA), reducing the maximum open probability and positively shifting the voltage dependence.
source: Besides the reported inhibition on Ca2+-dependent inactivation (CDI) (Liu et al., 2010; Singh et al., 2006; Wahl-Schott et al., 2006), several studies suggest that DCT also concurrently attenuates voltage-gated activation (VGA), reducing the maximum open probability and positively shifting the voltage dependence (Hulme et al., 2006; Lieb et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2016; Scharinger et al., 2015; Singh et al., 2008; Wahl-Schott et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: α1DS exhibits strong CDI and VGA.
source: Short variant of α1DS terminates shortly after the IQV motif and lacks almost entire DCT domain, and its Ca2+ current (ICa) exhibited strong CDI and VGA (Figure 1A).
evidence: Demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1A

claim: α1DS contains all the core elements for CDI including the IQV domain for apoCaM pre-association and the EF-hand motifs and N-terminal Ca2+/CaM binding NSCaTE motif for CDI transduction.
source: Regarding CDI, α1DS still contains all the core elements including the IQV domain for apoCaM pre-association and the EF-hand motifs and N-terminal Ca2+/CaM binding NSCaTE motif (Dick et al., 2008) for CDI transduction.
evidence: Supported by citation to Dick et al., 2008 and structural knowledge

claim: The value of 1−r50,Ca at −10 mV was taken as the index of CDI strength (SCa).
source: In practice, due to rather weak VDI of CaV1.3 at 50 ms (r50,Ba close to 1) (Tadross et al., 2010), thus for simplicity the value of 1−r50,Ca at −10 mV was taken as the index of CDI strength (SCa).
evidence: This is a methodological definition used in the study, with citation support

claim: JCa (Jpeak at −10 mV) served as the quantitative index for VGA.
source: Throughout this study, SCa and JCa (Jpeak at −10 mV) served as the quantitative indices for CDI and VGA respectively.
evidence: This is a methodological definition used in the study

claim: CDI of CaV1.3 is independent of global Ca2+ so insensitive to Ca2+-buffer capacities and variations in channel expressions.
source: Technically, compared to VGA and JCa, CDI and SCa are more robust so more favorable since CDI of CaV1.3 is independent of global Ca2+ so insensitive to Ca2+-buffer capacities and variations in channel expressions partly due to transient transfections (Dick et al., 2008; Tadross et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dick et al., 2008; Tadross et al., 2008

claim: α1DS-PCRD-DCRD exhibited substantially attenuated SCa and JCa compared with α1DS control.
source: Compared with α1DS control, SCa and JCa from α1DS-PCRD-DCRD were substantially attenuated, which provided ample dynamic ranges (highlighted by green areas) to explore CMI effects on CDI/VGA and its mechanisms (Figure 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1B

claim: Fusing only PCRD or DCRD onto α1DS resulted in no alteration in CDI in comparison with the α1DS control.
source: From all these channel variants, we concluded no alteration in CDI in comparison with the α1DS control, similarly from VGA results and analyses (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A

claim: All the three motifs of PCRD, DCRD and IQV are required for effective CMI.
source: Based on the fact that all the configurations under test failed to mediate SCa and JCa attenuations, all the three motifs of PCRD, DCRD and IQV might be required for effective CMI, consistent with the preliminary analyses on DCT subsegments from CaV1.3 and CaV1.4, in which the segment between PCRD and DCRD ('B' region) was dispensable but neither PCRD nor DCRD could be excluded (Liu et al., 2010).
evidence: Based on experimental data and supported by citation to Liu et al., 2010

claim: Under low [apoCaM], for the three α1DS-GX-DCRD variants, both CDI and VGA were concurrently and significantly attenuated.
source: Statistical summary of CDI (SCa) and VGA (JCa) in endogenous (control) or low [apoCaM] for all channel variants of α1DS, α1DS-PCRD and α1DS-GX-DCRD, with additional information in Figure 2—figure supplement 1. Notably, for the three α1DS-GX-DCRD variants, both CDI and VGA were concurrently and significantly attenuated. Statistical significance was evaluated and indicated (p<0.001, ***; p<0.05, *).
evidence: Demonstrated by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2D

claim: Only DCRD and IQV are required by CMI so that PCRD becomes dispensable if [apoCaM] is low.
source: Hence, mechanistically only DCRD and IQV are required by CMI so that PCRD becomes dispensable if [apoCaM] is low, unveiling the differential roles of PCRD and DCRD in the potential cooperation for CMI induction.
evidence: Based on experimental data showing CMI effects under low apoCaM conditions

claim: The trio of PCRD, DCRD and IQV failed to attenuate CDI when they were separately expressed as three individual peptides.
source: However, the trio failed to attenuate CDI when they were separately expressed as three individual peptides (Figure 3A–C), even when PCRD, DCRD and IQV (contained in α1DS) were all well expressed in the same cell as confirmed with fluorescent tags (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 3A–C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: When [apoCaM] was reduced with chelator BSCaMIQ, CDI remained ultrastrong for all the three test groups with separate peptides.
source: When [apoCaM] was reduced with chelator BSCaMIQ as in Figure 2, CDI remained ultrastrong and indistinguishable from α1DS control for all the three test groups (Figure 3D–F), and VGA analyses came to the same conclusions consistently (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D–F).
evidence: Demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 3D–F and Figure 3—figure supplement 2D–F

claim: All three combinations (I, II, and III) of linking any two modules out of the three exhibited CMI.
source: Interestingly, all the three combinations exhibited CMI, strongly attenuating both CDI and VGA as illustrated by green areas indicating the altered r50 and Jpeak profiles compared to α1DS control (Figure 4A—C).
evidence: Demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 4A—C

claim: PCRDD and PCRDF from CaV1.3 and CaV1.4 are interchangeable for CMI.
source: Combination I also provided a great chance to revisit the assumption we made earlier regarding interchangeable PCRDD and PCRDF from CaV1.3 and CaV1.4, respectively. Instead of dealing with two different channel variants, here the same α1DS served as the control to reliably evaluate PCRDD-DCRD vs PCRDF-DCRD peptides. And our assumption was validated by the negligible differences in VGA and CDI between the two PCRD-DCRD peptides (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: DCRD bound IQV-PCRD with higher affinity (Kd = 1135) than that between DCRD and IQV (Kd = 4700).
source: Live-cell FRET two-hybrid assays demonstrated that DCRD bound IQV-PCRD with higher affinity (Kd = 1135, units in donor-cube fluorescence intensity) than that between DCRD and IQV (Kd = 4700), regardless of whether PCRD as the standalone peptide was also present (Kd = 4624) (Figure 4D).
evidence: Demonstrated by FRET binding assay data shown in Figure 4D

claim: DCRD overexpression nearly abolished the binding between apoCaM and IQV-PCRD.
source: Owing to the high affinity between DCRD and IQV-PCRD, DCRD overexpression nearly abolished the binding between apoCaM and IQV-PCRD (i.e., apoCaM/channel pre-association) as demonstrated in the plot of FR-Dfree (FRET ratio vs free donor concentrations) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: Demonstrated by FRET binding assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A

claim: Without the presence of PCRD, apoCaM was still able to bind IQV, but the DCRD perturbation was much less effective.
source: meanwhile, without the presence of PCRD, apoCaM was still able to bind IQV, but the DCRD perturbation was much less effective (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated by FRET binding assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B

claim: If any two components have enough spatial closeness or intimacy, it would be sufficient for the third component to form the 'trio' complex and thus induce effective CMI.
source: Taken together, a cooperative scheme of CMI under physiological [apoCaM] in the cell was unveiled by functional and binding analyses (Figure 4E), which depicted that if any two components have enough spatial closeness or intimacy, e.g., by prearranged linkage, it would be sufficient for the third component to form the 'trio' complex and thus induce effective CMI (combinations of I, II and III, highlighted in grey ellipses).
evidence: Based on synthesis of experimental data from functional and binding analyses

claim: Rapamycin application induced rapid attenuation of both CDI (SCa) and VGA (Ipeak) within tens of seconds.
source: In contrast to the stable time-course profiles of the control group (Figure 5B), CDI (SCa) and VGA (Ipeak) were both rapidly attenuated upon applying 1 μM rapamycin. Within tens of seconds, dimerization between FKBP-DCRD with PCRD-FRB started to attenuate ICa as evidenced by time-dependent decays (Figure 5C).
evidence: Demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 5B,C

claim: Rapamycin induced strong CMI effects on ICa within 4–5 min in version 2, with SCa reaching 0.41 ± 0.06 and Ipeak reaching 35% ± 3%.
source: More potently than the earlier design but in a similar time course (version 1, Figure 5B,C), rapamycin induced strong CMI effects on ICa within 4–5 min (version 2, Figure 5E,F). Both CDI and VGA were substantially attenuated: SCa (0.41 ± 0.06, n = 5) and Ipeak (35% ± 3%, n = 5).
evidence: Demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 5E,F

claim: The current amplitude at 300 ms (I300) stayed at the same levels during the whole time course of rapamycin-inducible CMI, in contrast to rapidly decayed Ipeak.
source: One interesting feature we discovered from rapamycin-inducible CMI was that the current amplitude at 300 ms (I300) stayed at the same levels during the whole time course (Figure 6A, top two rows), in contrast to rapidly decayed Ipeak as outlined by blue dotted lines.
evidence: Demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 6A

claim: In the run-down process or the blockage by isradipine, both Ipeak and I300 were attenuated.
source: In the run-down process (Kepplinger and Romanin, 2005) or the blockage by isradipine (Anekonda and Quinn, 2011), the number of functional channels was reduced, which resulted into attenuations on ICa during the whole depolarization step including both Ipeak and I300 (Figure 6A, lower two rows).
evidence: Demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 6A, with citation support

claim: SCa remained constant for α1DS undergoing run-down or blockage since intrinsic gating properties of each channel were not altered.
source: In contrast, SCa remained constant for α1DS undergoing run-down or blockage since intrinsic gating properties (e.g., CDI) of each channel were not altered, whereas SCa was attenuated in CMI (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A

claim: I300 remained at similar amplitudes for all channel variants tested, regardless of whether CMI was in effect.
source: By revisiting different channel variants tested earlier, we concluded that I300 indeed remained at similar amplitudes for them all (Figure 6B), whereas their Ipeak and SCa exhibited broad dynamic ranges.
evidence: Demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 6B

claim: The constant I300 essentially set the lower limit for CMI.
source: The constant I300 (or J300) essentially set the lower limit for CMI. That said, while CMI potency was getting higher, Jpeak was tuned down to more closely approach J300 (e.g., Figure 6B vs Figure 1B).
evidence: Based on analysis of experimental data across multiple figures

claim: CMI attenuation on CDI is realized by reducing Ipeak while maintaining the end-stage ICa (indexed with I300 or I1000), which ensures the overall Ca2+ influx is reduced.
source: Even though, we just clarified that CMI attenuation on CDI is actually realized by reducing Ipeak while maintaining the end-stage ICa (indexed with I300 or I1000), which ensures the overall Ca2+ influx is reduced.
evidence: Based on synthesis of experimental data showing constant I300 and reduced Ipeak

claim: The interactions within the trio complex of IQV/PCRD/DCRD were largely unaffected by Ca2+/CaM produced from ionomycin-introduced Ca2+ and endogenous CaM.
source: To exclude potential complications from ambient Ca2+/CaM, we performed FRET experiments to ensure that the interactions within the trio complex of IQV/PCRD/DCRD were largely unaffected by Ca2+/CaM produced from ionomycin-introduced Ca2+ and endogenous CaM, although Ca2+/CaM indeed exhibited higher binding affinity to IQV than apoCaM (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Demonstrated by FRET experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3

claim: Under CMI of different potency, ICa from α1DS, α1DL, or α1DS with inducible peptide dimerization exhibited distinct Ipeak, SCa and Ca2+ influx.
source: Under CMI of different potency, ICa from α1DS (no CMI), α1DL (intermediate CMI), or α1DS with inducible peptide dimerization (ultrastrong CMI), exhibited distinct Ipeak, SCa and Ca2+ influx (Figure 7A—C, left) (green areas indicating the reduction of Ca2+ influx).
evidence: Demonstrated by computational modeling data shown in Figure 7A—C

claim: The time rates of Ca2+ oscillation and autonomous spiking in the SNc model were tuned down to different levels in accordance with ICa attenuations or CMI potencies.
source: Meanwhile, the time rates of Ca2+ oscillation and autonomous spiking in the SNc model were also tuned down to different levels in accordance with ICa attenuations or CMI potencies (Figure 7A—C).
evidence: Demonstrated by computational modeling data shown in Figure 7A—C

claim: Moderate (28%) blockade clearly reduced overall Ca2+ influx and resulted in similar attenuations in oscillation and pacemaking in the SNc model.
source: In parallel, we also simulated the conventional blockage in the CaV1.3/SNc model (Figure 7D). Similar attenuations in oscillation and pacemaking were observed from the SNc model when the moderate (28%) blockade clearly reduced overall Ca2+ influx (green area), supporting the current strategy to develop PD therapeutics based on conventional CaV1.3 antagonists (Gudala et al., 2015; Hurley et al., 2013; Kang et al., 2012; Pasternak et al., 2012).
evidence: Demonstrated by computational modeling data shown in Figure 7D, with citation support

claim: Ca2+ influx via CaV1.3 serves as the major index to determine the downstream of oscillation/pacemaking.
source: Collectively, one common rule was deduced for CMI, CDI and other modalities of inhibition: Ca2+ influx via CaV1.3 serves as the major index to determine the downstream of oscillation/pacemaking, i.e., reduction of Ca2+ influx leads to attenuation of pacemaking whereas enhancement of Ca2+ influx causes augmentation of pacemaking.
evidence: Based on synthesis of computational modeling results

claim: CMI essentially reduces Ca2+ influx, local and cytosolic Ca2+ concentration, and oscillation and pacemaking, all of which are potentially subject to bidirectional tuning under pathophysiological conditions.
source: In this context, CMI, emerging as one key regulatory mechanism distinct from others, essentially reduces Ca2+ influx, local and cytosolic Ca2+ concentration, and oscillation and pacemaking, all of which are potentially subject to bidirectional tuning under pathophysiological conditions.
evidence: Based on synthesis of experimental and computational data

claim: For LTCCs, gating inhibition by carboxyl-tail motifs (CMI) seems to be a universal mechanism preventing excessive Ca2+ influx and intracellular Ca2+ overload.
source: For LTCCs, gating inhibition by carboxyl-tail motifs (CMI) seems to be a universal mechanism preventing excessive Ca2+ influx and intracellular Ca2+ overload.
evidence: Based on inference from experimental data across CaV1 family members

claim: In CaV1.1 and CaV1.2 channels, C-termini of α1 subunits are subject to proteolytic cleavage and the site of cleavage is located between PCRD and DCRD.
source: In CaV1.1 and CaV1.2 channels, C-termini of α1 subunits are subject to proteolytic cleavage and the site of cleavage is located between PCRD and DCRD (Abele and Yang, 2012; Hulme et al., 2005, 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Abele and Yang, 2012; Hulme et al., 2005, 2006

claim: CMI provides direct evidence that attenuation of CDI via endogenous factors and mechanisms is essentially a reduction of Ca2+ influx.
source: Here we provide direct evidence that attenuation of CDI via endogenous factors and mechanisms is essentially a reduction of Ca2+ influx, assured by the fixed level of Ca2+ current at the late phase of ICa, i.e., I300 measured in this work, remaining the same regardless of the changes in Ipeak or SCa.
evidence: Based on experimental data showing constant I300 across conditions

claim: CaV1.3 acts as the dominant factor underlying subthreshold oscillation and pacemaking activities in SNc dopaminergic neurons.
source: CaV1.3 acts as the dominant factor underlying subthreshold oscillation and pacemaking activities in SNc dopaminergic neurons, although the detailed mechanisms are not fully elucidated (Chan et al., 2007; Durante et al., 2004; Putzier et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chan et al., 2007; Durante et al., 2004; Putzier et al., 2009

claim: Activity-dependent engagement of CaV1 channels elevates mitochondrial oxidant stress and vulnerability of SNc neurons, contributing to disease progression of PD.
source: It is currently believed that activity-dependent engagement of CaV1 channels elevates mitochondrial oxidant stress and vulnerability of SNc neurons, contributing to disease progression of PD (Guzman et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Guzman et al., 2010

claim: CaV1 blockers for hypertension treatment appear to reduce the risk of PD.
source: Additional support also comes from clinical evidence that CaV1 blockers for hypertension treatment, e.g., 1,4-dihydropyridines (DHPs) appear to reduce the risk of PD (Pasternak et al., 2012; Ritz et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Pasternak et al., 2012; Ritz et al., 2009
